comment: Ground truth for the user's own library (established by ear + analysis). Values are DETECTOR-relative: rot = allowed values of (downbeat index % beatsPerBar) on the detector's own beat grid; bpb = expected beatsPerBar. null = no stable ground truth, report only. reject:true = the detector must return null (no steady pulse deserves a metronome). barLenAt = [{t, n}]: the bar covering time t must be n beats long — the only anchor that catches an un-modelled meter change (a uniform-4 grid reports 4 everywhere and silently stretches the odd bar). Sourced from the published score AND verified against the audio before being committed.

Mr Crowley.note: slip-class song; two harmonic phase slips (126.6s, 166.5s) re-phased since v9 — anchor minted from the harmonically-validated grid (chord changes 86% on bar starts)

Nothing Else Matters.scoreNote: Ultimate-Guitar official score: 6/8 with 3/8 bars at bar 7 (intro), 57/73/117 (end of each chorus, on "Oh, but I know") and 142/147 (outro); dotted-quarter = 72. Our grid is 154 bars, ALL 6 beats. NOT anchored: at the chorus ends the score points to, our bars measure a clean 5.92-6.17 beats — no short bar — so either we absorb the 3/8 invisibly (which would shift bar phase by half a bar afterwards) or the score bar numbers do not map where assumed. The three stretched bars we DO have (198.93, 201.25, 317.07) sit in instrumental/outro regions, and the outro is where the score puts its last two 3/8 bars. Revisit when the bar decoder lands — this is the one score-vs-audio disagreement in the set and it needs an ear, not more arithmetic.

Sixteen Tons.note: harmonic re-phase v9: plain grid explained 4.6% of chord changes, re-phased 59% — anchor from the harmonically-validated grid; EAR-CHECK PENDING

Turn The Page.note: barAtMl = the bass-solo bars (201-227s spliced span), ear-approved 2026-08-01: the v14 span-phase vote lands them on the bass chord changes (margin 0.73; blind extension missed by ~1.5 beats; the model alone only half-bar-marks here). The 225s +2-beat re-entry odd bar remains the v5 fermata case.
Turn The Page.scoreNote: Official Metallica bass tab (D# G# C# F#, "Moderately Slow" quarter = 76; ours reads 74.9 — right octave): 112 bars, 4/4 at bar 1 and NEVER AGAIN. This is the counter-example the bar decoder needs — a song with five stretched bars that are NOT meter changes and must stay 4 beats. The barLenAt entries above pin exactly those five spots and pass today; they exist to fail if a decoder starts inventing odd bars wherever the tracker wobbles. OPEN QUESTION: we emit one 2-beat bar at 224.99 which the score does not have. That is the "+2 beats at the last chorus" the v5 fermata mechanics were built around, measured from the audio — a transcription normalises what a live-feel performance breathes, so score and recording may both be right. Needs an ear before it becomes an anchor either way.

Wanted Dead Or Alive.note: beatAtMl = the 48-93s drum-void the v8 gate refuses: v10 coasted through it and drifted up to half a beat (user heard it); v11 splices the model lattice there — ear-approved 2026-07-31. Anchors are BEAT times from the approved grid (coasting misses them by 330/335/104ms). v9's 204.8s breakdown re-phase rode along in that listen.

Cat Stevens — Father and Son.note: Ultimate-Guitar official score: 4/4 with 5/4 at bar 19 and 3/4 at bars 30, 41, 60; quarter = 67. Bar 19 spans "still"@66.20 -> "not"@70.55 = 4.94 beats at our 0.880 s beat, so the extra beat is in the audio, not just the page. v17 emits 58 bars, all 4 beats, and lands a bar line at 68.22 INSIDE the 5/4 bar — every downbeat after it is off, and the per-segment rotation vote thrashed (3,0,3,2,2) trying to fit uniform 4/4 to a song that changes meter. The 3/4 bars are not time-anchored yet.

Wild World.note: MSB full score: quarter = 74 (our 76.9 confirms the OCTAVE — the pre-v16 156.6 was wrong), 4/4 with 2/4 bars at 12, 29 and 46, one at the end of each verse. Two chords per bar (Am D / G C / F Dm), which is why the chord-change cue is structurally half-bar periodic here and cannot name the "1". v17 emits 59 bars, all 4 beats. A 2/4 bar shifts the phase by exactly 2 beats — the "which half-bar is the 1" ambiguity is a real meter change, not a tie. No time-anchored bar yet: the score is a different lyric transcription from ours, so word-level anchoring was unreliable (measured 7.07 beats where the score implies 6). Needs an ear verdict before anchors are minted.
